title: Ordinary quotient adjunction and normalized derived completion models
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and a scheme W with the independent site and coefficient universes of the project [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Use completed integral coefficient modules and finite scalar extension [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], the actual coefficient sequence module category and its exact restriction U to towers [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], and the coherent coefficient calculus S [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put tower=U on complexes and ordinaryLimit=lim U. An OrdinaryModel consists of an additive tensor functor T to sequence modules, normalized finite scalar-extension evaluation isomorphisms, the actual quotient transition equations, T adjoint to ordinaryLimit, and its unit sending x to the family of tensors 1 tensor x. It also records the canonical comparison from termwise ordinaryLimit to the limit of the tower complex, with its actual degreewise projections. Define quotient by applying T termwise, transpose by the termwise adjunction followed by that comparison, and augmentation as the transpose of the identity. A DerivedModel for S and an OrdinaryModel records the termwise tower-limit comparison, the ordinary-to-derived limit unit normalized by rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso on every K-injective tower, and the normalized isomorphism from the strict Roos model [def-weil-strict-roos-model] to this derived limit. It records a system comparison invertible on K-injectives and equal to the composite through exact restriction; and a universal left-derived comparison from S.reduction to termwise quotient, invertible on flat-term K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], with the specified finite evaluations and whole-Hom normalization. Define coneAugmentation by augmentation followed by the existing strict Roos inclusion. Define completionComparison by the Roos isomorphism followed by inverse exact-restriction and left-derived comparison isomorphisms. These are structures and real composites, not assumed existence assertions, and add no property to the inputs.
